answer_core:
I would not grant Marcus 15% equity plus a board seat now. Treat the demand as dependency-system design, not immediate package pricing: the question is whether the company can become stronger with Marcus, not whether his opening number is acceptable.

Friday should keep the discussion staged. No full equity, title, or board commitment until there is sprint evidence on platform delivery, team continuity, knowledge transfer, client delivery, governance behavior, and exit story. The 90-day sprint is useful if it tests whether Marcus grows enterprise capability while reducing single-person concentration.

That means keeping intermediate instruments alive: smaller equity without a board seat, milestone grants, phantom equity, platform revenue share, or a platform-specific upside path. It also means naming the relationship risk directly. Legal clauses will not remove Marcus's practical leverage if he owns the code relationship and can pull Jake or Lina.

Do not hide behind vague delay or a flat refusal. A vague delay or refusal may trigger Marcus disengagement and Jake/Lina/platform/client continuity risk. Make the conversation about the company Friday wants to run, what partnership would require from both sides, and what measurable proof would justify a larger commitment later.
